item: the machine record says which SQLCipher build runs: crypto provider, its version, and whether memory security is on (R470, D4)
summary: versions.sqlcipher_build = {provider, provider_version, memory_security}, each a string or {unavailable: <exception class>}, none left out. The provider pragmas need a keyed connection, so the reading opens a throwaway in-memory database with a random raw key that is kept nowhere, never the corpus passphrase, and fails closed: if keying raises, all three fields are unavailable with the class. cipher_memory_security is only read, never set. Why: the Windows holds of 36 to 68 s have no explained cause, and memory security (a locked-page call on Windows) is the one lever that could be 100 times slower there; the version string alone was identical on the Linux and Windows machines. Cost in the bundle: 154 bytes real, at most 416 (R470 byte exception, inside the R426 bound).
